propositions.justification: orders.create_order() has verified edges to both db.session and db.connection_pool while also synchronously invoking auth.verify(), inventory.reserve(), and payment.charge(); downstream latency can hold database resources for the duration of the order request, allowing concurrent order creations to exhaust the orders pool.
propositions.predicted_signal: orders database pool wait time rises and connection timeout errors appear on POST /orders during auth, inventory, or payment latency spikes.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() calls payment.charge() on the synchronous order-creation path; if payment timeouts or 5xx responses trigger order-level retries without coordinated backoff, repeated POST /orders retries can amplify load into payment and related dependencies.
propositions.predicted_signal: payment request volume spikes in synchronized bursts after payment timeout errors, with elevated retry attempts from POST /orders.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() invokes payment.charge() as part of order creation, but the graph shows no order-level idempotency guard before downstream charge/reserve operations; concurrent duplicate POST /orders requests can both reach payment and inventory before either request records completion.
propositions.predicted_signal: Duplicate payment charges or duplicate inventory reservations appear for concurrent POST /orders requests using the same client order identifier.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() has a verified synchronous dependency on auth.verify(); auth verification failure or latency directly blocks order creation even if orders database, payment, and inventory are healthy.
propositions.predicted_signal: POST /orders returns 5xx or times out while auth verification latency or error rate is elevated.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() synchronously calls inventory.reserve(); inventory reserve latency or failure can propagate to POST /orders timeouts or 5xx while order database resources remain held.
propositions.predicted_signal: POST /orders failures correlate with POST /inventory/{item_id}/reserve latency or error spikes.

propositions.justification: orders.create_order() synchronously calls payment.charge(); payment charge latency or failure can propagate to POST /orders failures, and the order path has no asynchronous compensation edge visible in the dependency graph.
propositions.predicted_signal: POST /orders failures correlate with POST /payment/charge latency or error spikes.

propositions.justification: orders.list_orders() accesses db.connection_pool for the order list query; a slow list query or many concurrent list requests can occupy pool connections and delay other orders operations.
propositions.predicted_signal: Connection pool wait time increases on GET /orders and connection timeout errors appear during order-list traffic spikes.

propositions.justification: orders.list_orders() accesses db.session; if the order list query lacks indexes for its filters or lazily loads child records per order, the list endpoint can perform table scans or N+1 queries and hold the DB session longer.
propositions.predicted_signal: GET /orders shows high rows-examined counts or many small repeated queries per request.

propositions.justification: orders.list_orders() is the DB-backed order list path; if it computes offset or page boundaries over a changing order set, an off-by-one boundary calculation can duplicate or skip records at page transitions.
propositions.predicted_signal: Adjacent GET /orders pages contain duplicate order IDs or omit order IDs at page boundaries.

propositions.justification: orders.get_order() uses db.connection_pool per detail lookup; high detail traffic or slow order-detail queries can consume pool connections and delay other order requests.
propositions.predicted_signal: Connection pool wait time increases on GET /orders/{order_id} and timeout errors appear during high detail-read concurrency.

propositions.justification: orders.get_order() accesses db.session; if the order_id lookup is not indexed or order line items are loaded per row, the detail request can cause full scans or N+1 queries.
propositions.predicted_signal: GET /orders/{order_id} latency rises with high rows-examined counts or repeated child-record queries per detail request.

propositions.justification: payment.charge_payment() invokes payment.check_idempotency() and the charge flow later executes the charge; the idempotency check and charge execution are separate graph steps, so concurrent identical charges can both pass the check before either commits.
propositions.predicted_signal: Duplicate charge records appear for concurrent POST /payment/charge requests using the same idempotency key.

propositions.justification: payment.execute_charge() uses db.connection_pool; long payment processing or database lock waits hold pool connections, and concurrent charges can exhaust the payment connection pool.
propositions.predicted_signal: Payment database pool wait time and timeout errors increase on POST /payment/charge during charge processing spikes.

propositions.justification: payment.check_idempotency() queries db.session; if idempotency keys are not indexed, each charge performs a slow or full scan before execution, increasing payment DB session time.
propositions.predicted_signal: Idempotency lookup queries show high rows-examined counts and elevated POST /payment/charge latency.
